outputs.name: HLA alleles and their state in the tumor

renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: allele_count
  title: HLA alleles called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of HLA alleles LILAC called, with the number of distinct HLA genes beside it, and the bars rank the genes by allele count. It answers how complete the typing is.
    How to read: every HLA gene carries two alleles, so a gene with fewer calls has an incomplete typing. Check its supporting fragments in the table before using it to predict neoantigen presentation.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/lilac/README.md
  column: gene
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: alleles, by HLA gene
  headline: true

- component: figure
  id: allele_cn_bar
  title: Tumor copy number per allele
  description: |-
    Each point is a called copy of an HLA allele and its copy number in the tumor, coloured by HLA gene; a homozygous allele has two points. It answers whether the tumor kept both copies of each allele.
    How to read: a copy number near one for each allele of a gene is the intact state. An allele far below one has been lost in the tumor, so it can no longer present the neoantigens that depend on it. Open the table for the lost flag.
    Note: LILAC derives the copy number from the tumor to reference fragment ratio and the PURPLE copy number. No cut-off is drawn, because none is sourced.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/lilac/README.md
  visu_type: strip
  dict_kwargs:
    x: allele
    y: tumor_copy_number
    color: gene
    labels:
      allele: HLA allele
      tumor_copy_number: Tumor copy number
      gene: HLA gene

- component: table
  id: allele_table
  title: HLA alleles
  description: |-
    Each row is a called allele with the fragments that support it in the reference, the tumor and the RNA, its tumor copy number, a flag for an allele lost in the tumor and the somatic variants inside it. It answers which alleles are intact and expressed, and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: a lost or mutated allele cannot present the neoantigens it would, so filter on the lost flag first. Few RNA fragments on a present allele suggest it is not expressed.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: allele_id
